name: 46189-longdecode-dsv32awq685b-8gpu
hardware: 8x H100 80GB HBM3 -- one whole a3 node.
parallelism: TP=8, PP=1, DP=1, EP off, DCP off; one in-process engine. TP=8 is forced by capacity -- 373 GiB of weights is 46.6 GiB per card at TP8 and 93 GiB at TP4, which does not fit an 80 GB H100.
architecture: DeepseekV32ForCausalLM (model_type deepseek_v32), 685B-parameter MoE with multi-head latent attention, AWQ 4-bit gemm at group size 128, bf16 activations; 373 GiB in 135 shards. Every shape is in the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=8, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, 8 requests bounded, safety_seconds 5400. Eight streams and eight requests is one wave: every request is in flight from t=0, and the 10% phases round down to zero requests, so all eight are measured.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, 4096 prompt tokens in and exactly 4096 output tokens out with min == max on both, so nothing is sampled. Greedy, temperature 0.0, seed 20260619, through the `vllm_python` in-process backend.
purpose: A long-form writing assistant on a 685-billion-parameter model, eight concurrent users, long prompts and replies, one eight-GPU node.
launch:
model: QuantTrio/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp-AWQ
tensor-parallel-size: 8

# 4096 prompt + 4096 output = 8192 exactly. The window has no slack: a request one token over it
# is rejected, not truncated.
max-model-len: 8192

# 0.80, which is the value this otherwise-verbatim serve line came with. It was pinned at 0.90
# (the engine default) until 2026-08-23; the reason for moving it is the shared card, not the
# workload. `request_memory` tests FREE memory against `util x TOTAL` before anything is
# allocated, so 0.90 is a standing demand for 71.3 of 79.19 GiB on EVERY one of the eight cards,
# and any neighbour holding more than ~8 GiB on any single card fails bring-up outright:
#
#   ValueError: Free memory on device cuda:6 (6.2/79.19 GiB) on startup is less than desired
#   GPU memory utilization (0.9, 71.27 GiB).
#
# 0.80 asks for 63.35 GiB and tolerates ~16 GiB. It cannot bind: 373 GiB of weights is 46.6 GiB
# per card, and the latent KV this workload needs is 8 streams x 8192 tokens x 61 layers x
# (512 + 64) x 2 B = 4.9 GiB, so 63.35 - 46.6 = 16.7 GiB is ~3.4x the requirement.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.80

# Size the KV pool from the CHECKPOINT instead of from whatever the card happens to have free.
#
# 8 GiB, against a workload that cannot consume more than 4.8 GiB of it. Per token this model
# caches one MLA latent vector, `kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim = 512 + 64 = 576` at bf16, plus
# the sparse indexer's own fp8 k-cache of `index_head_dim + index_head_dim/128 x 4 = 132` bytes:
#
#   (576 x 2  +  132)  x  61 layers            =  78,324 B  =  76.5 KiB per token
#   8 streams x 8192 tokens = 65,536 tokens    =   4.78 GiB
#
# so 8 GiB is 1.67x the most this workload can ever hold and the pool cannot bind: no request is
# ever preempted for cache and the scheduler admits all eight streams either way.
#
# WHY PIN IT AT ALL, rather than let the engine profile. `determine_available_memory`
# (`v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:412`) returns this value early and skips the `memory_profiling()`
# block. That block asserts that free memory has not MOVED between the start and the end of the
# profile, unconditionally and with no way to relax it, and on this cluster the profile runs
# ~7 minutes into bring-up, immediately after a 373 GiB weight load — the single most expensive
# thing to have to throw away because a neighbour arrived or left. Pinning the reserve makes the
# whole run depend only on the startup gate above, which is checked in the first seconds.
kv-cache-memory-bytes: 8589934592
